chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from al-Ḥasan, from Zurʿah, from Samāʿah, who said:

I asked him about what invalidates wudu (ablution). He said: An occurrence of passing wind whose sound you hear or whose smell you detect; and rumbling in the belly, unless it is something you can restrain; and laughter during salat (prayer); and vomiting.

key_terms.الْحَدَثُ: ritual nullifying occurrence, here referring to what breaks wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الْقَرْقَرَةُ: rumbling or gurgling in the belly
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification before acts of worship
key_terms.رِيحَهُ: its odor, indicating detectable passing wind

ai.seo_question: What things invalidate wudu (ablution) according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses acts that invalidate wudu (ablution), mentioning audible or detectable passing wind, a form of abdominal disturbance unless it can be restrained, laughter during salat (prayer), and vomiting. It is significant in fiqh because it addresses practical rulings related to taharah and the validity of worship.
